turns.t: Right, Mr Gallagher. The booking note says 'contact of a TB case, wants checking'. Is that why you're here today?
It is, aye. My daughter made the appointment. I said I was grand, but she wouldn't hear it.
Good for her. Tell me what happened, from the start.
My father was diagnosed with TB last month. They told us in the hospital, and the nurse there said the family should all get looked at.
That must have been a shock. How is he doing, if you don't mind my asking?
He's on the tablets now, and he's in good form. Giving out about the hospital food, so he must be better.
Ha, always a good sign. And how about you? Have you noticed anything yourself, anything at all?
It's nothing really. I've a bit of a cough, that's all.
A bit of a cough. How long have you had it?
Two weeks, I'd say. It's a dry sort of thing, and it's worse first thing in the morning.
Is it a dry cough every time, or do you bring anything up?
Dry, mostly, it just tickles.
Okay. Anything else? Even something you think is silly.
My voice has gone a bit hoarse, since Monday. The wife says I sound like a corncrake.
A corncrake, lovely. Is that the only thing?
I'm a bit tired in the afternoons, but sure, I'm not twenty any more.
Mm. Tired in the afternoons, is that new, or has it been like that for a while?
It's been the past week or so. Maybe it's the early mornings with the lad's football.
Maybe so. Have you had any coughing up blood?
No, nothing like that. Not a spot.
Good, thank you. Let me ask about your general health. Do you have any conditions I should know about?
I've an underactive thyroid, years now, and a bit of eczema on my hands. That's the lot of it.
And for the thyroid, what do you take, and how much? Do you know the dose?
Levothyroxine, every morning. Maybe 75 micrograms? Or is it 100? I can't mind, to tell you the truth. The chemist fills the little box for me.
That's grand. We can check it on the system later. Any operations in the past?
My appendix out, when I was fifteen. A summer I'll never forget, I missed the whole of the county final.
Ha, a hard price. Now, I'm curious about something. Your father was diagnosed, and you've seen him recently. How much time would you spend with him each week?
Oh, every Sunday for dinner, a couple of hours. And I'd drop in on Wednesdays. But since the diagnosis I've stayed away, only the phone.
Sensible. Well, before I examine you, can I have the nurse give me the numbers she took earlier?
Of course, doctor. Blood pressure is 124/80, pulse 78 bpm, temperature 36.9 °C, oxygen saturation 98 %, and respiratory rate 16 breaths/min.
Ahhhh.
Your throat looks a little red at the back, nothing dramatic. Now take some deep breaths in and out while I listen.
Your chest is clear all over, no crackles, no wheeze, and the air is going in well on both sides.
So I'll live, is that it?
I think you'll live for a good while yet. What I think is going on, and it is only my working view, is a post-viral cough, a lingering cough after a cold, with the hoarse voice that goes with it.
A cold? I never even had a cold. Well, the lad had one a few weeks back.
That would fit. Colds are often passed round the house, and the cough can hang on for weeks after the cold itself has gone.
And the TB? Does it rule it out?
I don't want you to feel I'm dismissing your father's illness, and being close to him was the right reason to come in. I'd just say that nothing I found today alarms me.
That's a relief, I can tell you. The wife has been at me. Is there anything I should do for the cough itself?
Plenty of warm fluids, honey and lemon is as good as anything, and rest your voice. Don't whisper, mind, because whispering strains it more than talking softly.
And if you ever start to cough up blood, or you get fevers and sweats at night, ring the surgery that day, don't wait.
I will, yes. I'd not wait with something like that.
I'd like to see you again in two weeks, to see how the cough and the voice are getting on. The desk will give you a time.
Two weeks, grand. Will I tell the daughter?
Tell her she did the right thing, and that she's earned a cup of tea off you.
She'll be delighted. Thanks, doctor, thanks, nurse.
Mind yourself, Mr Gallagher. Mind the puddle at the door.

symptoms.name: My voice has gone a bit hoarse
a bit tired in the afternoons

physical_examination.finding: throat looks a little red at the back

clinical_actions.description: Drink warm fluids, honey and lemon, and rest the voice
Ring the surgery the same day if coughing up blood or fevers and night sweats

clinical_uncertainties.description: The patient is unsure whether the levothyroxine dose is 75 or 100 micrograms.
